posts.title: Why CHRISTIAN Education? (And, Happy 35th Birthday to CHESS!!)
posts.summary: Reflecting on the foundations of Christian education and celebrating God's continuous provision over 35 years of ministry.
posts.body:
This year marks 35 years of Colorado Heritage Education School System — and we are deeply grateful to God for His faithfulness over every one of them.

## Why Christian Education?

The question is worth asking plainly. Why should a family choose Christian education? Why build an entire school system around biblical conviction?

The answer begins with a simple premise: **all truth is God's truth.** Education is never neutral. Every curriculum, every worldview, every approach to learning carries assumptions about the nature of reality, the purpose of human beings, and the source of moral authority. Christian education simply makes those assumptions explicit — and anchors them in Scripture.

We believe that God has entrusted the education of children to their parents. Not to the state, not to institutions, and not to culture. To parents. CHESS exists to come alongside families who take that responsibility seriously.

## 35 Years of Faithfulness

When Colorado Heritage was founded in 1991, homeschooling was a fringe movement. Families who chose to educate at home did so with limited support, uncertain legal standing, and very few resources. CHESS was built to change that — to give homeschooling families a private school home, accountability, and community.

Thirty-five years later, we have served hundreds of families across Colorado, the United States, and internationally. We have watched children grow into graduates, graduates grow into parents, and parents return to enroll their own children.

That is God's provision. We do not take it for granted.

## Looking Forward

As we enter our 36th year, our commitment remains unchanged: to partner with families in the noble pursuit of a Christ-centered education. To provide structure without rigidity, accountability without control, and community without compromise.

Thank you for being part of this story.

*"Pursuing the Knowledge of God."*

posts.title: Who Stole the Lost Tools of Learning?
posts.summary: An evaluation of modern pedagogy contrasted with the beautiful classical and Christian educational frameworks.
posts.body:
Dorothy Sayers asked the question in 1947. It remains just as urgent today.

## The Trivium and What We've Forgotten

Classical education rests on a framework called the Trivium: Grammar, Logic, and Rhetoric. These are not simply subjects — they are stages of learning that correspond to the natural development of the child's mind.

- **Grammar** (roughly ages 9–11): The child absorbs facts, language, and foundational knowledge with remarkable ease.
- **Logic** (roughly ages 12–14): The child begins to question, argue, and reason. This is the age of "why."
- **Rhetoric** (roughly ages 15–18): The young adult learns to express truth persuasively, with grace and conviction.

Modern education largely abandoned this framework in the 20th century. The result, Sayers argued, is students who have been taught *what* to think but not *how* to think.

## The Christian Distinctive

Classical education without Christianity produces eloquent pagans. The Trivium equips the mind — but the mind must be oriented toward something. At Colorado Heritage, we believe that something is the knowledge of God.

Every subject, rightly taught, points to Him. Mathematics reveals the order He built into creation. Literature explores the human condition He designed. History traces His providential hand through time. Science uncovers the mechanisms of a world He spoke into existence.

This is not a constraint on education. It is its completion.

## What This Means for Homeschooling Families

You do not need a classical school to give your children a classical education. Many of our Independent School families use classical curricula at home — and our Academy classes are designed to complement that approach.

The tools of learning have not been lost. They have simply been set aside. We invite you to pick them up again.

posts.title: Do You Love Jesus?
posts.summary: A heartfelt appeal to parents and educational shepherds on preserving Christ-first devotions in our daily educational structures.
posts.body:
It is a simple question. But it is the question that everything else depends on.

## The First Thing

In our zeal to provide excellent education — rigorous academics, strong transcripts, well-prepared graduates — it is possible to lose sight of the first thing. Jesus asked Peter three times: *"Do you love me?"* He did not ask: *"Are your students prepared for college?"* He did not ask: *"Are your records in order?"*

He asked: *"Do you love me?"*

We believe that Christian education begins and ends with this question. Not because academics don't matter — they do. Not because structure and accountability are unimportant — they are essential. But because all of it flows from this: a genuine love for Jesus Christ that shapes how we see the world, how we teach our children, and why we do what we do.

## For the Parents

You are not simply a curriculum manager. You are a shepherd. The children in your home are watching you — not just what you teach, but how you live. They are learning whether faith is a compartment or a foundation.

This is not a burden. It is the most important work in the world.

## For Our Community

At Colorado Heritage, we want to be more than a record-keeping service or an academic program. We want to be a community of families who are genuinely pursuing the knowledge of God together — who encourage one another, pray for one another, and hold one another accountable to the first thing.

Do you love Jesus? Let everything else flow from there.

# Why Christian Parents Should Take an Active Role in Educating Their Children

## The Greatest Influence in Your Child's Life Isn't a Teacher—It's You

Every parent wants their child to succeed. We want them to grow into responsible adults, develop strong character, achieve meaningful goals, and most importantly, know and love the Lord.

But in a culture that increasingly outsources nearly every responsibility, many parents have been led to believe that education is something best left to professionals.

Scripture paints a very different picture.

Throughout the Bible, God consistently places the responsibility for a child's education and discipleship on parents.

Deuteronomy 6:6–7 commands:

> "And these words that I command you today shall be on your heart. You shall teach them diligently to your children..."

Notice that God did not give this responsibility primarily to governments, institutions, or even churches. He gave it to mothers and fathers.

Christian education begins in the home because children belong first to God and are entrusted to their parents.

## What Actually Makes Someone Successful?

Many people assume success comes primarily from intelligence, talent, expensive schools, or academic credentials.

While those things can be helpful, study after study has shown that one of the strongest predictors of long-term success is parental involvement.

Children thrive when their parents are actively engaged in:

* Their education
* Their character development
* Their spiritual growth
* Their daily habits
* Their friendships
* Their goals and aspirations

When parents know what their children are learning, help them overcome challenges, and consistently invest in their development, children tend to perform better academically, socially, emotionally, and spiritually.

This shouldn't surprise Christians.

God designed families to be the primary training ground for future generations.

The home is where children learn discipline, responsibility, diligence, respect, wisdom, and faithfulness.

These qualities often matter far more in adulthood than test scores alone.

## The Biblical Model of Education

Christian parents have a unique calling.

Education is not merely the transfer of information. It is the formation of a person.

Every educational system is teaching more than math, science, reading, and history. It is teaching a worldview.

The question is not whether children will be discipled.

The question is who will disciple them.

Will they be shaped primarily by social media, entertainment, peers, and cultural trends?

Or will they be shaped by parents who intentionally point them to Christ?

The biblical model has always involved parents taking ownership of their children's formation.

Christian education should help children learn to think God's thoughts after Him, understand His world, and prepare for lives of faithful service.

## Why More Families Are Choosing Homeschooling

Homeschooling has grown dramatically over the past decade, and for good reason.

Parents increasingly recognize the benefits of being directly involved in their children's education.

Some of the advantages include:

### Stronger Family Relationships

When parents spend meaningful time teaching and mentoring their children, relationships deepen.

Instead of only seeing one another during rushed mornings and evenings, families spend more time learning and growing together.

### Individualized Learning

Every child learns differently.

Homeschooling allows parents to adapt education to their child's strengths, weaknesses, interests, and pace.

### Greater Flexibility

Families can schedule vacations, mission trips, service projects, internships, and educational experiences without being tied to a traditional school calendar.

### Biblical Integration

Christian parents can naturally integrate Scripture and a biblical worldview into every subject.

Children learn that Christ is Lord over all of life—not just Sunday mornings.

## The Challenge Many Parents Face

Even parents who love homeschooling often encounter a challenge:

"I want to stay involved, but I also need support."

Many parents desire the best of both worlds:

* Active parental involvement
* Academic support
* Community and friendships
* Accountability
* Experienced instructors

This is exactly where hybrid homeschool programs can be incredibly valuable.

## How CHESS Helps Parents Stay Involved

At CHESS, we believe parents should remain the primary educators of their children.

Rather than replacing parents, we come alongside them.

One of the biggest advantages of CHESS is our two-day-per-week class model.

Students attend classes only two days each week, allowing families to retain the flexibility and parental involvement that make homeschooling so effective.

This approach offers several benefits.

### Parents Remain the Primary Influence

Children spend the majority of their educational time under the guidance and supervision of their parents.

Instead of surrendering educational responsibility, families maintain ownership of the learning process.

### Professional Instruction and Support

Students benefit from qualified teachers and structured classroom experiences while parents receive additional support and resources.

### Strong Christian Community

Families gain access to friendships, encouragement, and community with other Christian families pursuing similar goals.

### Flexibility for Family Life

The two-day model provides room for family activities, discipleship, service opportunities, travel, entrepreneurship, extracurricular activities, and real-world learning experiences.

### A Partnership, Not a Replacement

CHESS exists to strengthen what parents are already doing—not replace them.

We believe parents know their children best and play the most important role in their long-term success.

## Success Begins at Home

When we look at Scripture and experience, the conclusion is clear:

The most influential factor in a child's life is often not a curriculum, a classroom, or a teacher.

It's an engaged parent.

Children thrive when mothers and fathers actively invest in their education, character, and faith.

Christian parents have a unique opportunity to shape the next generation—not merely for academic achievement, but for faithful service to Christ.

At CHESS, we are committed to helping families do exactly that.

Through a flexible two-day-per-week model, supportive Christian community, and a commitment to parental involvement, we help parents remain at the center of their children's education while providing the support they need to succeed.

Because the goal isn't simply raising educated children.

It's raising faithful, capable, Christ-centered adults who are prepared to serve God in every area of life.
posts.title: Why Christian Parents Should Take an Active Role in Educating Their Children
posts.summary: Christian parents have been given the primary responsibility for educating and discipling their children. While schools, churches, and teachers can provide valuable support, Scripture consistently places the responsibility for a child's training on mothers and fathers. Research likewise demonstrates that parental involvement is one of the strongest predictors of a child's long-term academic, social, and personal success.
